subject: Instrumentation gating, metrics access and temporary latency exemption request
messages:
From: Samantha Klein <sam.klein@crescenthealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@crescenthealth.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Instrumentation gating, metrics access and temporary latency exemption request

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement started our SLO review and attached the standard questionnaire (crescent-slo-questionnaire.pdf). A few items we want clarified up front so our security and infra teams can sign off:

1) How do you compute availability and latency SLOs (aggregation window, sampling)?
2) Are p95/p99 computed across all production inference requests, or are internal warming / retry attempts excluded?
3) What monitoring/alerting tooling do you surface to customers? Can we get a read-only dashboard or API to pull metrics?
4) We have a planned migration window (database cutover) the week of Jul 6 that will increase tail latency for ~2 hours per day. Would you consider a temporary SLO relaxation/exemption for that window, and what controls would you require?

Can you send a short summary and any quick artifacts (metrics spec, dashboard access instructions) so I can move this to our security team? Ideally we have something by Monday so procurement can include it in the package.

Thanks,
Samantha Klein
Senior IT Procurement
Crescent Health

Attachment: crescent-slo-questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Klein <sam.klein@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation gating, metrics access and temporary latency exemption request

Samantha —

Appreciate the questionnaire. I've attached a short summary (redwood-slo-measurement-summary.pdf) that answers 1–3 and lists the dashboards we can provide. Short answers here while Marissa and Jonas weigh in on the exemption flow: 

- Availability: measured as successful-inference / total-inference sampled at 60s buckets. We compute an hourly rolling availability and surface the 30-day percentage for contractual checks.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 measured on end-to-end inference time (request enter -> final token emitted). We exclude synthetic warm-up traffic and internal retry attempts flagged by the request_id header.
- Aggregation & sampling: default collection is 1s granularity in our internal telemetry, rolled into 1-min and 1-hour windows for dashboards and SLO evaluation. We sample traces for atypical flows; raw request-level data retention policy is 30 days.
- Alerts: customers get alerts (email + webhook) for SLO breaches and high-error spikes; we have configurable thresholds per alert rule.
- Metrics access: we can grant read-only Grafana invites and a metrics API token scoped to the account. I included the dashboard-invite.txt with instructions for self-service invite and the endpoint for metrics pulls.

Jonas / Marissa — can you confirm the standard procurement exception path for temporary latency relaxation and whether Redwood can implement a per-account temporary policy (time-bound) plus compensating controls (priority routing / cache pinning) for Crescent?

Next steps: I can get the Grafana invite issued within 24 hrs and share the logs / p99 computation notebook if needed.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-slo-measurement-summary.pdf (application/pdf); dashboard-invite.txt (text/plain)
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Klein <sam.klein@crescenthealth.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation gating, metrics access and temporary latency exemption request

Hi Samantha / Karthik —

On Fri, Jun 19, 2026 at 09:12 AM Samantha Klein <sam.klein@crescenthealth.com> wrote:
> We have a planned migration window (database cutover) the week of Jul 6 that will increase tail latency for ~2 hours per day. Would you consider a temporary SLO relaxation/exemption for that window, and what controls would you require?

Quick technical proposal from the infra team below. We're okay to support a temporary, scoped SLO relaxation under the following conditions: 

1) Scope & duration: a time-bound exception for up to 2 hours/day for up to 4 consecutive days (we can extend to a weekly 2-hr window for a 4-week cutover with renewed sign-off). We prefer the latter (4-week window) if Crescent expects recurring migration steps.
2) Metric carve: we will exclude requests tagged with header X-Maintenance-Window: crescent-mig from SLO evaluation for the defined window. Crescent must add this header to traffic during the migration period.
3) Compensating controls: require read-only Grafana access (we'll provision a dashboard with p95/p99, availability, error-rate and a maintenance tag filter), and a webhook to receive alert notifications.
4) Capacity mitigation: we can provision burst capacity at a negotiated commit for the migration days (temporary dedicated instances) — cost to be discussed with procurement.
5) Audit & rollback: we will produce a weekly digest during the exception period that shows traffic volumes, excluded requests, and any error/latency spikes. If we see >3x baseline errors or unresolved high-error spikes we reserve the right to pause the exception.

Action items: 
- Crescent: confirm whether the migration is a daily 2-hr block for 4 weeks or 2 hrs across 4 consecutive days; confirm who will set the X-Maintenance-Window header.
- Karthik: please prepare the temporary-policy amendment and procurement-friendly language for the statement of work; include the invoice delta for burst capacity.
- I'll provision the Grafana read-only panel and a metrics webhook once we have signed confirmation.

I'll leave Marissa on for commercial sign-off if procurement requires contractual language.

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Klein <sam.klein@crescenthealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@crescenthealth.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation gating, metrics access and temporary latency exemption request

Thanks Jonas — this is exactly the detail procurement and our SRE folks needed.

We confirm: it's a weekly 2-hour maintenance block on weekdays for four weeks starting Jul 6 (roughly 02:00–04:00 local). We will ensure the X-Maintenance-Window header is applied by our gateway team and will share the contact (gw-ops@crescenthealth.com).

Next items for procurement: 
- Please send a short amendment (one paragraph) that we can attach to the contract describing the temporary exception and the monitoring / rollback conditions.
- Send the Grafana read-only invite to sam.klein@crescenthealth.com and gw-ops@crescenthealth.com.
- Share the cost estimate for burst capacity for the scheduled windows.
- DocuSign would be easiest for our legal team — can you provide the amendment there?

If you can get the amendment and Grafana invite this week we can close procurement before month-end.

Best,
Samantha

Attachment: procurement@crescenthealth.com (email group)
